fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is pre-oxidation of an unspecified HEA, whereas the target intervention is increasing Mo content in an SPS-fabricated CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
The proposed -50 to 500 °C range and general sliding conditions do not match the target dry-air tests from room temperature to 800 °C against Si3N4 under specified load, speed, and distance.
ZrTiO4 is imported from evidence on an AlCrTiZrMo film and is not chemically relevant to the target CoCrFeNiMo composite or its NiO/silver-molybdate glaze.

The evidence does not establish simultaneous friction and wear reductions across the claimed temperature range; some cited evidence concerns tribocorrosion, and E5 reports oxide formation increasing friction.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad self-lubricating HEA problem and proposes a testable treated-versus-untreated comparison. Its oxide-film mechanism has limited conceptual overlap with the target's high-temperature protective tribofilm, but it misses the central Mo-composition intervention, solid-solution and sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature silver-molybdate glaze formation. The baseline and operating boundaries are vague, with no alloy composition, oxidation schedule, load, counterface, speed, or sliding distance. The experiment could falsify the proposed alternative, although stronger discrimination would require fixed treatment parameters, replication, temperature-specific acceptance criteria, and chemical identification of the retained tribofilm. The citations support oxidation resistance or oxide-assisted lubrication only in particular systems and environments, not the broad claim made here.
